headline: Protein language models extend to interactions, modifications, and modified peptides
label: Protein Language Model Methods
summary: Pretrained sequence representations are now applied to protein-protein interactions, PTM syntax, enzymes, and peptide developability in recent work.
synthesis: The common thread is adapting sequence-based learned representations to task-specific prediction. ProtSyntax applies a PTM-aware protein language model with geometry-constrained attention to 40 PTM-site benchmarks and PTM crosstalk, and EnzGFM uses an enzyme-specific Mamba-Transformer hybrid for catalytic property prediction. MSA Pairformer, at 111M parameters, extends AlphaFold-style pairwise refinement to protein-protein interaction coevolution. PeptiVerse and LINKER accept modified-peptide SMILES or ligand SMILES alongside sequence, moving beyond canonical amino acids. PepCL adds replay-based continual learning to update peptide-MHC class I predictors with new assay data. What is new is the breadth of targets rather than a single architecture. DB-IRES uses a CNN, BiGRU and self-attention ensemble, and the scaffold gap-filling work uses an ML ensemble with beam search.
